subject: maths
title: KS1 Maths diagnostic (test fixture)
curriculum: National Curriculum in England, KS1 mathematics (test fixture only, not a real assessment)
intro: Your tutor will read each question with you & help you start.

skills.name: Counting and place value
skills.why: Knowing what each digit is worth is the base for every other part of maths.
skills.strong: {name} counts confidently and knows what each digit in a number is worth.
skills.developing: {name} counts well but is still unsure what the tens digit is worth.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet secure counting past 20. This holds up adding and taking away, so it is worth fixing now.
skills.next_step: We will use counting games and number lines until it feels easy.

skills.name: Adding and taking away
skills.why: Quick, accurate adding and taking away makes every later topic lighter work.
skills.strong: {name} adds and takes away accurately, even with bigger numbers.
skills.developing: {name} adds small numbers well but slows down when crossing ten.
skills.gap: {name} is finding adding and taking away tricky at the moment. Most of maths builds on this, so it comes first.
skills.next_step: We will build number bonds to 10 and 20 with lots of short practice.

skills.name: Times tables and sharing
skills.why: Times tables unlock fractions, division and a lot of problem solving later.
skills.strong: {name} already knows the 2, 5 and 10 times tables well.
skills.developing: {name} understands groups of things but does not know the tables by heart yet.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet confident with groups and times tables. These come up again and again, so they are worth practising now.
skills.next_step: We will learn the 2, 5 and 10 times tables with patterns and games.

skills.name: Measuring and money
skills.why: Measuring and money connect maths to everyday life, which builds confidence.
skills.strong: {name} compares lengths and works with money confidently.
skills.developing: {name} compares lengths well but is less sure with money.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet sure how to compare lengths or count money. These are everyday skills, so they are worth securing.
skills.next_step: We will measure real objects and count real coins together.

questions.stem: Which of these is the same as 2 groups of 5?

questions.explain: 1 metre is 100 cm, which is longer than 90 cm.

questions.stem: Sam has 14 sweets. He eats 6. How many sweets are left?
How many pence are there in £1?
What is the 4 worth in the number 47?
questions.explain: The 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 40.
16 + 4 = 20. The others mix up adding and taking away, or tens and ones.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers are in the 5 times table?
questions.explain: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5: 15 and 30.

questions.stem: You have two pencils. Explain how you would find out which one is longer.

rubric.criterion: Says to line them up side by side, starting at the same point
Mentions measuring each one with a ruler, in centimetres

questions.explain: Either method on its own earns 1 mark.
